clue.text: Fuss if father stands in front of basin

indicators.note: the father piece is placed ahead of the basin piece in the answer

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
a laver is a washing basin, especially in a church

explanation.surface: A father plants himself before the sink and makes a scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A palaver is a tiresome to-do or commotion, the same as a fuss.

clue.text: Reasonably good-looking?

definitions.meaning: as an adverb meaning fairly or moderately, as in 'fairly good'
attractive in appearance, as of a face

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark hints that the two words are separate senses rather than one phrase meaning 'quite handsome'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word works both as an adverb meaning fairly and as an adjective meaning attractive.

clue.text: Sounds as if Scots landowner was in retreat

indicators.note: the clue says the landowner's title is heard, not written, giving a near-identical spoken word

parts.note: a laird is a Scottish landed proprietor

explanation.surface: A Scottish estate owner seems to have withdrawn from public life.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal that lay in its lair was holed up in its den, that is in retreat.

clue.text: I anger a vet disposed to be a selective eater

indicators.note: disposed means arranged or set out, so these letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A vet is cross because an animal refuses some foods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposed' rearranges the letters of I ANGER A VET.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who avoids meat chooses carefully what to eat, a selective eater.

clue.text: The teacher wanting to chatter endlessly

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter of the chatter word is dropped

parts.note: to rabbit (on) is British slang for to talk at length

explanation.surface: An educator who does not care for idle gossip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' removes the T from RABBIT. In British slang to 'rabbit on' is to chatter.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbi is a Jewish religious teacher; the title literally means 'my master'.

clue.text: They believe hold-up occurred in back street

indicators.note: in means the robbery word is placed inside the turned street letters
back means the street abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: a heist is a robbery or hold-up

explanation.surface: A robbery took place in an alley behind the shops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the street abbreviation round to TS, so the robbery sits between those two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Theists are people who hold a belief in God.

clue.text: Expression silver worker applied to harridan

parts.note: a term is a word or expression
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
a worker ant is the stock crossword worker

explanation.surface: A silversmith's phrase is directed at a nagging old woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A termagant is a scolding, overbearing woman, a synonym for a harridan.

clue.text: Test half the flex before midday

indicators.note: before puts the half word ahead of the time abbreviation
half the means only the back two of the four letters of flex are used

parts.note: AM (ante meridiem) means before midday

explanation.surface: An electrician checks a cable in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half the' takes the second half of FLEX; 'midday' stands for the morning abbreviation, since AM means before noon.
explanation.definitionFit: An exam is a formal test of knowledge.

clue.text: Slattern gets first-class return to the country

parts.note: a sloven is an untidy, slovenly person

indicators.note: return means the first-class letters are read backwards

parts.note: A1 means first-class, read as the letters AI

explanation.surface: A slovenly woman is flown home in first class.
explanation.definitionFit: Slovenia is a central European nation, the country meant.

clue.text: View article in a state of fury

parts.note: to view is to see
an article is an item or thing

explanation.surface: Seeing a certain item makes someone livid.
explanation.definitionFit: Seething describes boiling with anger, being furious.

clue.text: Looking, say, to encompass Chinese principle

indicators.note: to encompass means the example letters wrap round the Chinese principle

parts.note: eg (for example) is signalled by say
yin is the passive principle in Chinese philosophy

explanation.surface: Someone is investigating a tenet of Chinese philosophy.
explanation.definitionFit: Eying is watching or gazing at, which is looking.

clue.text: A song to sing in unadorned surroundings

indicators.note: surroundings means the plain word encloses the singing word

parts.note: bare means plain or unadorned
to carol is to sing joyfully

explanation.surface: A song is performed in a plain, undecorated setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to sing' looks like part of the definition, but it is the verb that goes inside the plain word.
explanation.definitionFit: A barcarole is a Venetian gondolier's song.

clue.text: Claire, that rendition was dramatic!

indicators.note: a rendition is a version or rendering, so these letters are given a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone praises Claire's over-the-top performance of a piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rendition' rearranges the letters of CLAIRE THAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatrical means showy and exaggerated, as dramatic behaviour is.

clue.text: Network takes note quietly

parts.note: me (mi) is a note of the tonic sol-fa scale
sh is the call to be quiet

explanation.surface: A broadcaster quietly takes down a message.
explanation.definitionFit: A mesh is a net or web of interlaced strands.

clue.text: Navigators plot it to gain entrée

definitions.meaning: sailors chart a route across the open sea, the main
the principal dish of a meal, in American usage

explanation.walkthrough: The 'main' is the open sea, so a sailor's route across it fits the first reading.
explanation.definitionFit: In the US an entrée is the principal dish of a meal.

clue.text: Announcement made by Roman coal pit

indicators.note: made by means the following letters are worked into something new

explanation.surface: A Roman colliery publishes a public notice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made by' rearranges the letters of ROMAN COAL PIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A proclamation is a public, official announcement.

clue.text: Old warrior's protection against importunate letters

definitions.meaning: armour of interlinked metal rings worn by knights
pestering letters that demand to be copied and sent on

explanation.walkthrough: 'against' is only a link joining the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Linked-ring armour and pestering chain letters share the same name.

clue.text: Odds on the second one making a splash

parts.note: SP is the starting price, the odds in horse racing
the latter is the second of two

explanation.surface: A horse's odds mean the runner-up causes a stir.
explanation.walkthrough: SP, the starting price, is the British betting abbreviation for the odds on a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A splatter is a messy spattering, a splash.

clue.text: It once pressed novice to tuck into tart

indicators.note: to tuck into means the beginner word goes inside the tart word

parts.note: a flan is an open tart
a tiro is a beginner or novice

explanation.surface: A trainee is told to eat a pastry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to tuck into' looks like eating the tart, but it puts the beginner inside the pastry; TIRO is a crossword favourite for a novice.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned heated iron was used to press clothes.

clue.text: Cheat orders a quick pint

definitions.meaning: read literally, asks the barman to draw a beer quickly

explanation.walkthrough: In a pub a barman pulls a pint from the pump, hence the second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to trick someone, and literally a fast-drawn pint.

clue.text: Work in section for modern paintings

indicators.note: in means the work abbreviation sits inside the section word

parts.note: a part is a section
op (opus) is a work

explanation.surface: A piece in a gallery's section for contemporary art.
explanation.definitionFit: Pop art is a 1950s-60s movement of paintings drawing on popular culture.

clue.text: After conflict, Edward becomes worn

indicators.note: after means the Edward abbreviation follows the conflict word

parts.note: a fray is a fight or conflict
Ed is short for Edward

explanation.surface: After the battle, Edward is exhausted.
explanation.definitionFit: Frayed fabric is threadbare, that is worn.

clue.text: In Grandma's time they drank sparkling wine

indicators.note: in means the letters are found within the words grandma's time

explanation.surface: Back in Grandma's day people drank fizz.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' signals that the answer sits within GRANDMA'S TIME.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a sparkling white wine from Piedmont.

clue.text: Hardly smelling of roses

parts.note: read literally a bad smell; figuratively being out of favour

explanation.definitionFit: Being in disfavour is the opposite of coming up smelling of roses.

clue.text: Get old Christian books from middleman

parts.note: to age is to get old
NT is the New Testament

explanation.surface: An ageing man takes Christian books from an intermediary.
explanation.definitionFit: An agent acts as a go-between, a middleman.

clue.text: Watch struggle by centre forward

parts.note: to vie is to compete or struggle

indicators.note: centre means the middle letter of forward is used

explanation.surface: A striker in the middle of the attack battles while spectators look on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre forward' looks like a football position, but means the middle letter of FORWARD, W.
explanation.definitionFit: To view is to watch or look at.

clue.text: Finish repairing entire mat

indicators.note: repairing means fixing, so these letters are put back in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone completes the job of mending a whole rug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repairing' rearranges the letters of ENTIRE MAT.
explanation.definitionFit: To terminate is to end or finish.

clue.text: Prepared to study before May's end

indicators.note: before puts the study word ahead of the final letter

parts.note: to read is to study

indicators.note: end means the last letter of May's is taken

explanation.surface: Getting ready to revise before the end of May exams.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready means prepared.

clue.text: We learn about the Renaissance

indicators.note: about means scattered around, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A history student is learning about the Renaissance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges the letters of WE LEARN.
explanation.definitionFit: A renaissance is a revival or rebirth.

clue.text: Shouted when given medical care

definitions.meaning: in British slang, to shout someone is to buy them a drink

explanation.walkthrough: 'Shouted' is the slang sense of paying for a round, not raising one's voice.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both having paid for others and having been cared for medically.
